note: THE VECTOR SET of the door's policy document (REG-1.86; REG-4.131), in the registry bodies' one scheme: the document's WHOLE CONTENT is one object, type admission-policy, under the canonical rule -- parse(b) answers a policy only where b == encode(parse(b)) -- and it is no deposit: it carries no sig and no kind. `parse` is the parse's answer, `ok` or the refusal's cause as skep-registry's ParseRefusal::token spells it; on an admitted document `approval_hand` is what its READER answers for the approval's hand: `officer`, `unattended` (auto, honored only where admission is open), or null where the approval value is one the parser does not know, which opens no approval (REG-4.108). THE CAP is the registry records' own, 16,384 bytes, as every registry body but a request is held to: a document past it answers past_cap, ahead of every other stage -- before its text, its JSON or its members are read. AN EMPTY DOCUMENT IS NO POLICY: a door whose policy document is absent, holds no version, or whose standing version this parse refuses is shut alike for every reader -- no request admitted, no approval -- so the `empty` vector's refusal is that door's whole answer.
